title: Every non-abelian p-group has a non-inner automorphism of order p
credit: Y. Berkovich (Kourovka Notebook Problem 4.13); survey by Sarkar–Joshi
premise_risks: Naming: usually called the 'non-inner automorphism conjecture', but some papers call it 'Berkovich's conjecture'. The owner may treat it as person-named.
Possible incremental partial results in 2025-26 that I did not find; no resolution claim found
plain: Every group acts on itself by conjugation, and these 'inner' automorphisms are its obvious symmetries. Does every finite non-abelian group whose order is a power of a prime p have an automorphism that is not inner and that gives the identity when applied p times? Gaschütz proved in 1966 that a non-inner automorphism of p-power order always exists, but getting order exactly p has resisted proof for decades.
math: For every prime $p$ and every finite non-abelian $p$-group $G$, prove that there exists $\varphi\in\mathrm{Aut}(G)\setminus\mathrm{Inn}(G)$ with $\varphi^p=\mathrm{id}$ (such a $\varphi$ has order exactly $p$), or find a counterexample.
